subject: Renewal: provisioning for 24k-context model + reranker add-on
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@elasticcommerce.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — larger model + reranker needs

Hi Karthik,

As we look to renew our Dedicated contract in March, we've had two engineering initiatives surface that will materially change our inference needs:

- Move to a 24k-context retrieval-augmented generator (planning to test "orca-24k" next month).
- Add a reranker pipeline post-retrieval (low-latency top-k reranks at high QPS).

Both of these increase per-request GPU memory and steady-state throughput. We pulled last-quarter traffic (attached) and expect a 2.5x increase in peak token throughput during campaigns.

Can we set up a short call next week to review capacity options, SLA impacts, and draft amendment language? We're trying to decide between expanding our reserved pool vs adding a dedicated burst pool for reranks.

Attached: traffic_report_q4.csv

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Director of ML Platform, Elastic Commerce

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@elasticcommerce.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — larger model + reranker needs

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the data.

High-level I think there are three levers: 1) add reserved H100 capacity (scale), 2) carve a dedicated low-latency pool for reranks (isolation), and 3) introduce a burst/spot pool for campaign spikes.

Can you confirm the following before we draft an amendment?
- Expected steady-state qps for generator and reranker separately (p95 and peak)
- Typical request tokens and max context used in production (generator + retrieved context)
- Any hard latency SLOs for the reranker (p95/p99)

Marissa / Priyom — looping you in to weigh in on recommended pool sizing and an ops ramp plan. I'll hold a 30-min slot next Fri if that works for Sarah.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@elasticcommerce.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — capacity recommendation (internal + customer)

Hi all — dug into Sarah's traffic and sketched a pragmatic config we'd recommend. See attached capacity_plan_v2.xlsx for the math. Summary below: 

- Recommended reserved pool: +6x H100s dedicated to generator inference (24k context). This preserves latency for baseline traffic and supports the generator model memory footprint.
- Reranker strategy: carve a 3x H100 dedicated low-latency pool (smaller batch sizes, pre-warmed KV-cache) to hit p95 <= 120ms for top-k reranks at expected qps. Separate the pool to avoid noisy-neighbor impact on generator workloads.
- Burst pool: 4x smaller instances (mixed A100/H100 depending on region) with autoscale policy for campaign spikes; configured with fair-share throttles and fallback to a cheaper, lower-context model for overflow.
- Throughput guarantees: propose a contract amendment with two SLO tiers — "Committed" (99.5% availability, p95 latency targets) for reserved pools, and "Best-effort" for burst pool.
- Ramp schedule: immediate +30% capacity at renewal effective date, full ramp to target over 6 weeks with a staged canary deploy. Ops runbooks and warmup window included in the attachment.

Risks/notes: quantization for the 24k generator may reduce peak memory, but will increase CPU host-side work — we included conservative headroom. Pricing estimates included in the spreadsheet.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_plan_v2.xlsx

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@elasticcommerce.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@elasticcommerce.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity recommendation (procurement looped)

Thanks, Marissa and Karthik — that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups from our procurement and engineering teams:

- Procurement: can you provide 12/24-month pricing tiers for the committed H100 counts and the dedicated reranker pool? Would you consider a 24-month lock for a ~12% discount vs 12-month?
- Engineering: we confirm target p95 for reranker must be <= 120ms, and steady-state reranker qps ~ 1,800 with campaign peaks to 4,500 for short bursts (10-15 mins). Generator steady-state qps ~ 600 with 3x campaign spikes.

If the pricing tiers and a short-form amendment look reasonable, procurement would like a draft SLA and a statement of work for the ramp.

Sarah
Sarah Lin
Director of ML Platform, Elastic Commerce

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@elasticcommerce.com>, Procurement <procurement@elasticcommerce.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed amendment & pricing options — RDW-5231

Hi Sarah / Procurement team — please find our proposed amendment summary below and attached the short-form SLA (proposed_sla_amendment.pdf) and a DocuSign link for signature. Summary: 

- Committed capacity (option A, 12-mo): +6x H100 reserved for generator; +3x H100 reserved for reranker; burst pool on-demand. Monthly committed fee: $78,500.
- Committed capacity (option B, 24-mo): same counts; 12% term discount applied. Monthly committed fee (24-mo): $69,080.
- Throughput & latency SLOs (for reserved pools): p95 reranker <= 120ms, p95 generator <= 300ms; availability 99.5% monthly. Credits for SLO misses per SLA table (see attached).
- Ramp & execution: upgrade begins at renewal effective date. Week 0: provision reserved nodes and run compatibility tests. Week 1–3: staged canary; Week 4–6: full traffic migration. Ops playbooks and rollback plan included.
- Add-on: optional model-mix clause — if Elastic switches to a larger model (e.g., >24k context or an additional reranker flavor) within the term, we will conduct a capacity re-evaluation and propose a pro-rated amendment for additional reserved capacity.

Next steps: we'll post the DocuSign link and the amendment in the Redwood contract portal (link below). If procurement signs option B (24-mo), we'll schedule the ops kickoff and commit the pool provisioning windows.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/link/abc123
Redwood amendment doc: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/amendments/RDW-5231

Please reply with preferred term (12 vs 24) and any edits to the SLA.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_sla_amendment.pdf
